clue.text: Treacly stuff produced by Maureen and the girls

parts.note: Mo is a common short form of the name Maureen
lasses is a northern British word for girls

explanation.surface: Someone credits a sticky treat to Maureen and her daughters' kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick dark syrup left over from refining sugar is the classic treacly substance.

clue.text: England's leader entering top cricket club, a revered place

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the club's initials, entering them

parts.note: the MCC, Marylebone Cricket Club, is the historic governing club of English cricket

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so this takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An England captain joins the leading cricket club, treated as hallowed ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'England's leader' gives E, which 'entering' puts inside MCC, the Marylebone Cricket Club based at Lord's in London; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca, the holiest city of Islam, is used for any place people flock to in devotion.

clue.text: Replying in anger, wins surprisingly

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome hints that the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone responds in a temper and unexpectedly wins the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges ANGER and WINS together; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering is responding to a question or remark, the same participle form as the clue.

clue.text: Uses foot to crush member of family

definitions.meaning: treads on something, as a phrase of two words
a husband's or wife's son from an earlier marriage

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means treads underfoot; as one, a child by marriage, a relative.

clue.text: Silly Adele is clapping biased argument

indicators.note: silly behaviour is muddled, so these fifteen letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The singer Adele foolishly applauds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges all of ADELE IS CLAPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Special pleading is a one-sided argument that cites favourable points and ignores unfavourable ones.

clue.text: Increases disapproving utterances around the street

indicators.note: the jeers are placed around the road abbreviation, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: boos are noises a crowd makes in disapproval

explanation.surface: Jeering in the road grows louder.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to raise or lift it, a verb in the same form as the clue's third person.

clue.text: The effect of Venus's fly trap as a plant?

definitions.text: The effect of Venus's fly trap
definitions.meaning: the carnivorous plant catches insects, so they are lost
a bristly flowering herb of the borage family

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words it describes insects disappearing; whole, it names a herb. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects vanishing into a carnivorous trap is a disappearance of creepy-crawlies; whole, it is a blue-flowered herb.

clue.text: Severely criticized, having kept silver hidden

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is tucked out of sight inside the word for kept

parts.note: saved means kept or preserved
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A thief was condemned for having stashed away silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here it means one piece is tucked inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics who savage a work attack it fiercely, a past participle like the clue's.

clue.text: See a nerd travelling on river, one singing of love?

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Watch a geek drifting on a river, crooning a love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges SEE A NERD, and R follows; in a down clue 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song sung outdoors under a window, so the singer is a romantic performer.

clue.text: Stranded man wanting people in boat that much, we hear

indicators.note: a listener's phrase, telling the solver the letters come from how the words are spoken

parts.note: people working a boat are its crew, and that much means so, giving crew so

explanation.surface: A castaway who longs for company on a boat so badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, CREW and SO sound like the surname of Defoe's shipwrecked hero; 'wanting' is only a link that suits the castaway picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is the most famous fictional castaway, marooned alone on an island.

clue.text: English enthusiast for Durer, say

parts.note: English gives ENG
a raver is an enthusiastic, wild partygoer, so an enthusiast

explanation.surface: An English fan of the German Renaissance artist Albrecht Durer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'say' marks Durer as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Durer was celebrated for his copperplate and woodcut prints, so he is an example of a printmaker who cut plates.

clue.text: There's a sort of party and king in Persia's getting drunk

indicators.note: the single letter for the monarch sits inside the rearranged letters
someone drunk is unsteady and jumbled, so the letters of the country's name are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, including the s of the possessive
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Persian king throws a party where everyone ends up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' scrambles the country's name with its possessive s counted as a letter, and the king's letter goes in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Apres-ski is the social round of drinks and gatherings at a resort after skiing, so a kind of party.

clue.text: O for this help up a mountain!

definitions.meaning: O is the chemical symbol for this element
climbers at high altitude carry bottled gas to breathe

explanation.definitionFit: The element whose symbol is O is the gas mountaineers breathe from cylinders in thin air.

clue.text: Man gets to island lake in a particular area

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald
Iona is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A man travels to an island lake somewhere specific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' looks like the abbreviation I, but here it is a whole island, IONA, off western Scotland; 'gets to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional describes something confined to one district rather than the whole country.

clue.text: Denied split would tear apart imperial unit's core

indicators.note: the verb for tearing is opened up so another piece can be put inside it
the weight unit sits at the centre, the core, of the outer word

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
an ounce is a unit of weight in the British imperial system

explanation.surface: A rejected scheme to divide up the imperial weight measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words, 'split' and 'core', together signal that the weight unit sits in the middle of the tearing word; 'would' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to give up or disown something, so renounced fits denied in the sense of repudiated.

clue.text: Sun — had small boy to be protected from it?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday, here read as Sun
taken as written
Ed is a short form of a boy's name such as Edward

explanation.surface: A child had a day in the sun and needed covering up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's first word: 'it' is the sun, and something shielded from the sun's glare is in shade. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept out of direct sunlight under cover is in the shade.

clue.text: Previously mentioned idea so far looking unrealistic

indicators.note: something unrealistic is distorted from its true form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan that so far seems impractical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking unrealistic' rearranges IDEA SO FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a legal word for something already referred to earlier in a document.

clue.text: One in a million with five companions?

definitions.text: One in a million with five companions?

parts.words: One in a million with five companions
parts.note: the figure for a million is a 1 followed by six zero digits, so each zero has five others beside it

explanation.surface: Something rare that still has five friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a million' suggests something exceptional, but it is literal: one of the six zeros in 1,000,000.
explanation.definitionFit: Each zero in the written number for a million is one of six alike, so it has five fellow ciphers.

clue.text: Good person in university role seen as status seeker?

indicators.note: the saint abbreviation is placed inside the word for a role

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
St, for saint, stands for a good person

explanation.surface: A virtuous student takes a campus job and is thought a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good person' is the crossword shorthand for a saint, and 'in' places it inside the role.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen who acts with unearned self-importance, hungry for rank.

clue.text: Inferior support given to the board maybe

definitions.text: Inferior support given to the board maybe

parts.words: Inferior support given to the board maybe
parts.note: inferior is read as lower down: a frame standing beneath a table top, with board in its sense of a plank

explanation.surface: A second-rate endorsement offered to a company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests weak backing for a company board; really it is a frame that holds up a plank or tabletop from below.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of a beam on splayed legs, used in pairs to hold a tabletop.

clue.text: Felt bad about being surplus to requirements

indicators.note: a bad state is a disordered one, so the four letters are rearranged

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fretting over something

explanation.surface: Someone felt miserable about being made redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns the letters of 'Felt' into a word meaning departed; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or goods remaining once needs are met are spare, surplus to what was wanted.

clue.text: Frightened female gets a prolonged reprimand

parts.note: an earful is a long scolding

explanation.surface: A woman is scared after a lengthy telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; EARFUL follows F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearful means afraid or anxious.

clue.text: Like Paddington, from which you can get some tours in England

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A bear fond of travel in England, from which tour guides take a share.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'tours in England': tOURS IN England. 'from which you can get' links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a bear from Peru in British children's books, and ursine means bearlike.

clue.text: Tales can get edited for literary collection

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Stories may be revised for an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get edited' rearranges TALES CAN; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Analects are selected passages gathered from an author's writings, most famously those of Confucius.

clue.text: Piece of paper the man found in collection

indicators.note: the pronoun turns up inside the group word, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a set is a collection of things
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A document a man discovered among a batch of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single rectangular piece of paper.

clue.text: Man very good about not having drink or food

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man

indicators.note: the top-quality rating wraps around the abstainer's letters, enclosing them

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the figure 1 as the letter I
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A virtuous man who will take neither a drink nor a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very good' is A1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I; 'about' wraps that pair around the teetotal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is an Indian unleavened flatbread, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Country father, one of the forebears half forgotten

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: half of the word is left out, so only its first four letters remain

parts.note: an ancestor is one of a person's forebears

explanation.surface: A patriarch whose ancestral land is half lost to memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half forgotten' drops the back half of the eight-letter forebear word, leaving its first four letters after the priest's title.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation of western Europe.

clue.text: Case seen in appointment around 4

indicators.note: the meeting word is wrapped around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting or engagement
IV is 4 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A grammatical case turns up in a meeting set for four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the dative is the case marking an indirect object, as in Latin and German.

clue.text: Ancient duke in burst to find valuable stuff

indicators.note: the pair of pieces are put inside the sudden rush of wind

parts.note: a gust is a sudden burst of wind
old means ancient

explanation.surface: An elderly aristocrat bursts in to discover treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare and much prized is likened to precious metal powder, a common idiom for anything scarce.
